questions.text: CSS 2018, 2023, 2024 · Pair: Faint / Feint — Which meaning fits “Faint”?

options.A: To scatter or plant seeds; (noun) a female pig
options.B: To fire a weapon; a new growth from a plant
options.C: Weak, barely perceptible; or to lose consciousness briefly
options.D: A deceptive movement meant to mislead an opponent

questions.explanation:
Faint: Weak, barely perceptible; or to lose consciousness briefly. Sentence: "After standing for hours in the heat, the old man felt faint and sat down; the music was so faint we could barely hear it."
Feint: A pretended attack or movement meant to deceive an opponent. Sentence: "The boxer made a feint with his left hand and then struck with his right."
Source: CSS 2018, 2023, 2024 English Precis & Composition (cssaspirants.pk).

questions.text: CSS 2024 · Pair: Creak / Creek — Which meaning fits “Creak”?

options.A: A harsh, high-pitched sound, e.g. from an old door or floor
options.B: (Sailing) to shift a sail across the boat; (informal) to agree or be consistent with
options.C: A small stream or narrow inlet
options.D: Dry and withered (of plants or land)

questions.explanation:
Creak: A harsh, high-pitched sound, e.g. from an old door or floor. Sentence: "The old wooden door would creak loudly every time someone opened it."
Creek: A small stream or narrow inlet of water. Sentence: "The children waded across the shallow creek to reach the other bank."
Source: CSS 2024 English Precis & Composition (cssaspirants.pk).

questions.text: CSS 2024 · Pair: Palate / Palette — Which meaning fits “Palate”?

options.A: To escape or avoid someone or something cleverly; to be hard to grasp
options.B: A board on which an artist mixes colours
options.C: The roof of the mouth; a person's sense of taste
options.D: About to happen; very near in time

questions.explanation:
Palate: The roof of the mouth; a person's sense of taste. Sentence: "After years in Lahore, his palate preferred spicy food to bland dishes."
Palette: A thin board on which an artist mixes paints; a range of colours. Sentence: "The painter squeezed blue and yellow onto her palette to mix green."
Source: CSS 2024 English Precis & Composition (cssaspirants.pk).

questions.text: CSS 2024 · Pair: Elicit / Illicit — Which meaning fits “Elicit”?

options.A: A pretended attack or movement meant to deceive an opponent
options.B: To draw out a response, answer or reaction
options.C: (British, noun) a person who relies on another, especially financially

questions.explanation:
Elicit: To draw out a response, answer or reaction. Sentence: "The teacher's question elicited a lively discussion from the class."
Illicit: Illegal or forbidden by law, rules or custom. Sentence: "Customs officers seized a truck carrying illicit drugs at the border."
Source: CSS 2024 English Precis & Composition (cssaspirants.pk).

questions.text: CSS 2024 · Pair: Peal / Peel — Which meaning fits “Peal”?

options.A: A loud ringing of bells; a loud burst of sound
options.B: The outer skin of a fruit; to remove it
options.C: To disturb or unsettle someone's composure
options.D: A stone or concrete platform along water where ships are loaded and unloaded

questions.explanation:
Peal: A loud ringing of bells; a loud burst of sound. Sentence: "A peal of laughter rang through the hall when the comedian finished his joke."
Peel: The outer skin of a fruit or vegetable; to remove it. Sentence: "Peel the oranges and give the slices to the children."
Source: CSS 2024 English Precis & Composition (cssaspirants.pk).

questions.text: CSS 2024 · Pair: Taut / Taught — Which meaning fits “Taut”?

options.A: A short quotation at the start of a book or chapter; an inscription on a building or statue

questions.explanation:
Taut: Stretched or pulled tight; tense. Sentence: "The tightrope walker stepped onto the taut wire stretched between the poles."
Taught: Past tense and past participle of 'teach'. Sentence: "My grandfather taught me how to play chess when I was seven."
Source: CSS 2024 English Precis & Composition (cssaspirants.pk).

questions.text: CSS 2024 · Pair: Rheum / Room — Which meaning fits “Rheum”?

options.A: A watery discharge from the eyes or nose
options.B: A sledge drawn by horses or reindeer, used for travel on snow
options.C: A space or area that can be occupied
options.D: Not tight or firmly fixed; free (adjective)

questions.explanation:
Rheum: A watery discharge from the eyes or nose. Sentence: "The old man's eyes were red and full of rheum from his cold."
Room: A part of a building enclosed by walls; space. Sentence: "There was no room left on the bus, so we had to stand."
Source: CSS 2024 English Precis & Composition (cssaspirants.pk).

questions.text: CSS 2024 · Pair: Wreak / Reek — Which meaning fits “Wreak”?

options.A: To escape or avoid someone or something cleverly; to be hard to grasp
options.C: Carried or endured (past participle of 'bear' in other senses)
options.D: To cause or inflict great damage or harm

questions.explanation:
Wreak: To cause or inflict great damage or harm. Sentence: "The floods wreaked havoc on the villages along the Indus."
Reek: To smell strongly and unpleasantly; a strong bad smell. Sentence: "The rubbish dump reeked so badly that passers-by covered their noses."
Source: CSS 2024 English Precis & Composition (cssaspirants.pk).
